item.title: Revolut hacker: data from 700 Swiss customers
item.description: Hacker attack on Revolut: almost 700 Swiss customers hit. Criminals are asking for $3 million not to publish the data.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - **Revolut**, an online bank, suffered a hack that led to the delivery of data of almost 700 customers to cybercriminals. - Hackers posed as Italian authorities, putting pressure on Revolut. - No money was stolen, but sensitive data such as passport information and account numbers. - The incident mainly involves Swiss customers.
## Key facts - Hacker attack: Revolut provided data to cybercriminals. - Method: Hackers exploited an official Italian communication channel (PEC). - Compromised data: Passports, accounts and addresses of almost 700 customers. - Victims: especially Swiss customers. - Ransom: Hackers demand $3 million from Revolut not to publish the data.
The hacker attack on the online bank Revolut also affected Switzerland, involving a significant number of Swiss customers. The hackers acted in an unusual way, publishing their ransom demand on a website and addressing public opinion instead of negotiating directly with the company. This has raised questions about the real motivations of cybercriminals.
> "Normally hackers negotiate privately directly with their victims," explains Pascal Lago, SRF's economic editor. "Criminals then turn to public opinion rather than directly to the affected company. This raises a lot of questions, for example whether it is really just about money or whether the The hacker attack on Revolut raises concerns about the security of Swiss customers' personal data. The incident highlights the vulnerability of official communication channels, such as the Italian PEC, which can be exploited by cybercriminals to obtain sensitive information. This case highlights the need to strengthen security measures and raise users' awareness of the importance of protecting their personal data.
> "For this reason there is great nervousness in Italy," says Pascal Lago. "Hackers could also access the data of many other companies. For this reason, the Italian authorities are also investigating the case. "
The impact on Revolut's image in Switzerland could be significant, especially considering the recent banking license application. Swiss customers, who often use Revolut as an additional account for holidays abroad, may be discouraged by the incident and prefer other safer options. In addition, the incident could have repercussions on the trust of customers towards online banks in general, pushing them to prefer traditional institutions with physical branches.
The hacker attack also highlights the need for greater collaboration between Swiss and Italian authorities to counter cross-border cybercrime. Ongoing investigations in Italy could provide valuable information to prevent future similar attacks in Switzerland.

Following the hacker attack on Revolut, it is important for Swiss customers to take some precautions to protect their personal data. Here are some steps to follow:
### Data Security Verification Regularly check your Revolut account to verify any suspicious activity. If you notice anything unusual, immediately contact Revolut's customer service to report the issue.
### Personal Data Protection Ensure you have secure and unique passwords for your Revolut account and other financial services. Avoid sharing sensitive information, such as account numbers or passport details, unless absolutely necessary.
### Activity Monitoring Keep an eye on the transactions on your account and report any unauthorized activity. Revolut offers tools to monitor your spending and receive real-time notifications.
### Information and Updates Stay informed about the latest news regarding the Revolut hacking incident. The company should provide regular updates on the situation and the measures adopted to protect customer data.
### Changing Banks If you feel insecure or have doubts about the security of your data with Revolut, consider the possibility of changing banks. In Switzerland, there are many options to choose from, both traditional and online. Make sure to compare the different offers and choose an institution that meets your needs and guarantees the security of your data.
To help you make an informed decision, you can use our banking cost calculator to compare the fees and commissions of different Swiss banks. This tool will help you find the option best suited to your needs and budget.
Remember, the security of your personal data is fundamental. Taking the right precautions can help you protect your sensitive information and prevent potential fraud or identity theft.

item.title: Vaud Apprenticeship and Vocational Training
item.description: Complete guide on how to find an internship position in the Canton of Vaud: contract, apprenticeship salary and professional maturity.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Discover how to find an apprenticeship in the Canton of Vaud. - Information on contract, salary and vocational maturity. - Procedures and practical tips for apprentices.
## Key facts Apprenticeship contract: Mandatory Apprentice remuneration: Variable by sector and year Vocational maturity: Possible for many apprentices Apprenticeship duration: Varies according to profession
In the Canton of Vaud, the apprenticeship and vocational training pathway represents a privileged route for entering the labour market, offering young people practical skills and a solid foundation for their future career. Searching for an apprenticeship position requires a targeted approach that takes into account the specificities of the canton and the various professions available. The apprenticeship contract, a fundamental document that regulates the relationship between apprentice, employer and vocational school, must be signed before the start of training. This contract defines crucial aspects such as the duration of the apprenticeship, training objectives, working hours, remuneration and holidays.
The remuneration of an apprentice in the Canton of Vaud, as in the rest of Switzerland, is not set at federal level and varies significantly according to the professional sector, the year of training and the company’s wage policy. Generally, the salary increases progressively throughout the apprenticeship years. It is essential to inquire about average wages for the desired profession by consulting cantonal professional associations or dedicated vocational training guides. In addition to on‑the‑job training, the apprentice attends a vocational school where they acquire the necessary theoretical knowledge. For many professions, it is also possible to obtain the vocational maturity certificate, a qualification that opens the door to higher education at the Universities of Applied Sciences and Arts (UAS), further broadening career prospects. Admission procedures for the vocational maturity certificate vary, but often require passing specific exams at the end of the apprenticeship. The cantonal authorities of Vaud, through their vocational training offices, provide support and detailed information to guide young people and companies through this essential training pathway. ### Finding the ideal internship position The search for an internship position in the Canton of Vaud takes place through various channels. Cantonal professional associations and chambers of commerce play a central role, often publishing internship offers on their online portals or organizing fairs dedicated to vocational training. Vocational schools themselves also provide active support in the search, making available information about partner companies and available positions. It is advisable to start the search well in advance, usually a year before the expected start of the internship, as the most sought-after applications are often filled quickly. Preparing a complete and personalized application dossier, which includes a detailed curriculum vitae and a convincing motivation letter, is essential to stand out. An orientation interview or a trial period in a company can represent further steps in the selection process, allowing both the candidate and the employer to assess mutual suitability.
### The internship contract and remuneration Once the desired position has been identified, signing the internship contract is the next step. This legal document, drafted according to cantonal and federal directives, establishes the rights and duties of all parties involved. It must clearly state the profession of the internship, the total duration, the start and end dates, the workplace, the weekly working hours, the annual leave (which cannot be less than that provided for by the federal labour law, i.e. four weeks for adults and five for those under 20 years of age), the monthly remuneration and the payment terms. The remuneration of an apprentice in the Canton of Vaud, as mentioned, is highly variable. To give an idea, the first years of apprenticeship can foresee salaries ranging from a few hundred to over one thousand Swiss francs per month, with significant increases in the following years. The exact figures depend heavily on the sector (for example, an apprentice in an industrial sector may earn a different remuneration from one in a commercial office or a shop). It is always advisable to consult the indicative salary tables provided by the trade associations to obtain a more precise picture.

item.title: Permit L Graubünden: validity and extension
item.description: The L permit for Grisons is valid for up to 1 year, with the possibility of extension and transfer to B permit under specific conditions and constraints for the employer.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - L permit for Graubünden: validity up to 1 year. - Extension possible, but with limits. - Transition to B permit to be evaluated. - Constraints for the employer.
## Key facts Short-term permit: L Maximum duration: 1 year Extension: possible Transition to B permit: possible Employer requirements: yes
The short-term work permit, known as the L permit, is a type of residency authorization for foreign workers who intend to carry out gainful employment in Switzerland for a limited period, usually not exceeding one year. In the canton of Graubünden, as in the rest of the Confederation, the L permit is subject to specific regulations that define its duration, the conditions for extension, and the requirements for its possible renewal or transformation into a residence permit (B permit). Its issuance is strictly linked to a concrete job offer and to certain conditions that must be met by both the employee and the employer. The main objective of this permit is to facilitate the entry of foreign labour for temporary labour needs, without however creating an automatic right to long-term residence in the country. It is essential to understand that the L permit is not, by itself, indefinitely renewable; its nature is intrinsically temporary. The cantonal authorities of Graubünden, within their competence, carefully assess each individual application, taking into account factors such as the local labour market situation and the professional qualifications of the applicant. The expiry of the L permit obliges the holder to leave Swiss territory, unless the requirements for an extension or for the issuance of another type of permit are met. Procedures and requirements may vary slightly depending on the sector of activity and the nationality of the applicant, but the general principle of temporal limitation remains unchanged. Strict compliance with current regulations is essential to avoid future complications and to ensure the legality of the stay in Switzerland. Its validity is strictly tied to the duration of the employment contract or to the specific reason for which it was granted, and its expiry does not confer the right to remain in Swiss territory without further authorisation. The competent authorities of Graubünden are responsible for verifying the fulfilment of the requirements and deciding on the possible granting of extensions or transformations, always in compliance with federal legislation on foreigners and labour. The temporary nature of the L permit requires careful planning on the part of the foreign worker and his/her future employer, considering the long-term implications of staying in Switzerland. The management of the L permit in the Canton of Graubünden requires a careful assessment of the possibilities for extension and, in some cases, of transition to a residence permit (permit B). Although the L permit is intended for short-term stays, Swiss law allows, in specific and justified circumstances, its extension. However, it is crucial to understand that extensions are not automatic and are subject to an evaluation by the competent cantonal authorities. These authorities will verify whether the conditions that led to the initial issuance of the L permit still exist and whether there are new elements justifying an extension of the work stay. A fundamental aspect to consider is the link with the employer. Often, the extension of the L permit is conditional on the continuation of the employment relationship with the same company or on a new job that meets the requirements for this type of permit. In the absence of a valid job offer or if work needs cease, the extension is unlikely to be granted. For those who intend to settle more permanently in the Canton of Graubünden, the possibility of moving from an L permit to a B permit (residence) represents an option to consider. This transition entails a new application procedure and the demonstration of meeting more stringent requirements, such as the ability to support oneself economically independently and, for citizens of certain third countries, the absence of threats to security and public order. The change from L to B is not an automatic right and depends on the discretionary evaluation of the authorities, who will consider the individual situation of the applicant and the needs of the local labor market. It is important to emphasize that the application for conversion must be submitted before the expiration of the current L permit. Ignoring deadlines or failing to follow procedures may result in the need to leave Swiss territory. Consultation with the competent cantonal offices or with professionals experienced in foreign nationals' law is strongly recommended to navigate these procedures correctly and to plan as best as possible one's future work and stay in Switzerland, especially in a specific cantonal context like that of Graubünden, which may have administrative peculiarities linked to its size and economic structure.

La gestione del permesso L nel Cantone dei Grigioni implica una serie di passaggi pratici e adempimenti burocratici sia per il lavoratore straniero che per il datore di lavoro. Una volta ottenuto il permesso L, la sua validità è strettamente legata alla durata del contratto di lavoro sottoscritto. È essenziale che sia il lavoratore che il datore di lavoro ne monitorino attentamente la scadenza per evitare situazioni di irregolarità. Qualora si desideri prolungare il soggiorno oltre la durata originaria del permesso L, è necessario presentare una richiesta di proroga alle autorità cantonali competenti con un congruo anticipo rispetto alla data di scadenza. La documentazione richiesta per la proroga solitamente include una nuova offerta di lavoro o una conferma della continuazione del rapporto lavorativo, oltre a eventuali altri documenti che le autorità potrebbero richiedere per valutare la sussistenza dei presupposti per l'estensione. Se l'obiettivo a lungo termine è stabilirsi in modo più permanente nei Grigioni, è opportuno informarsi sulla possibilità di richiedere un permesso di dimora (permesso B). La transizione da un permesso L a un permesso B richiede la presentazione di una nuova domanda completa, che dovrà dimostrare il soddisfacimento dei requisiti specifici per il permesso B, quali ad esempio la stabilità economica e l'integrazione socio-professionale. Le tempistiche per queste procedure possono variare, ed è quindi consigliabile avviare le pratiche con largo anticipo. Per una corretta pianificazione e per assicurarsi di rispettare tutte le normative vigenti, è fondamentale consultare i siti ufficiali del Cantone dei Grigioni o rivolgersi agli uffici preposti all'immigrazione e al lavoro. La comprensione delle procedure, dei documenti necessari e delle scadenze è cruciale per evitare spiacevoli conseguenze. Per chi cerca di comprendere meglio la propria situazione retributiva e fiscale in Svizzera, è utile avvalersi di strumenti di calcolo specifici. Un [calcolatore dello stipendio](nav:calculator) può fornire una stima dettagliata delle trattenute e del netto percepito, aiutando a pianificare le proprie finanze in modo consapevole, tenendo conto delle diverse imposte e contributi previdenziali applicabili nel Cantone dei Grigioni e a livello federale. Questo strumento è particolarmente utile per chi si appresta a lavorare in Svizzera con un permesso di breve durata, per avere una chiara visione della propria situazione finanziaria.

item.title: Canton Vaud school system: enrolments and cycles
item.description: Complete guide to compulsory education in the Canton of Vaud: study cycles, age of enrollment, languages and transition to high school.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Compulsory schooling structured in specific cycles - Enrollment procedures based on children's age - Defined pathways for the transition to upper secondary schools - Languages of instruction regulated at the cantonal level
## Key facts Scope: Compulsory schooling Location: Canton of Vaud Elements: Cycles, enrollment, calendar, languages Objective: Transition to upper secondary schools
The school system of the Canton of Vaud is organized to guarantee compulsory education through a cycle-based structure, designed to accompany the student from childhood until the completion of compulsory studies. The organization is based on precise age criteria for enrollment and follows a school calendar coordinated at the cantonal level, which defines lesson periods and holidays.
### The organization of school cycles Compulsory schooling in the Canton of Vaud is not a single block, but is divided into cycles that allow for gradual pedagogical progression. Each cycle has specific learning objectives and requires age requirements for access. Enrollment usually takes place based on the child's date of birth, ensuring that every student is placed in the class corresponding to their age group.
Languages of instruction represent a fundamental pillar of the system. Since Vaud is a French-speaking canton, French is the main medium of instruction, but the system provides for the introduction of other languages to prepare students for a national and international context. The management of these linguistic skills is integrated into the programs of each cycle, facilitating the integration of students coming from different linguistic regions of Switzerland or from abroad.
The transition between the various cycles is monitored to ensure that the student has acquired the necessary skills. This path culminates with the transition to upper secondary schools, where students are oriented toward academic or professional pathways based on their aptitudes and the results obtained during compulsory schooling. ### Practical implications for families For those settling in the Canton of Vaud, understanding how school cycles work is essential for planning their children's integration. Enrollment is not a single formal act, but a process that follows the child's growth stages. A parent arriving in the canton must verify which cycle their child falls into based on age, as access is strictly linked to this parameter.
The impact of the school calendar directly affects family and work organization. Since holiday and festive dates are established at the cantonal level, residents must coordinate their commitments with school closing periods. This is particularly relevant for those working in other cantons or having partners with different calendars.
### Transition and orientation scenarios Consider the hypothetical scenario of a student completing the compulsory education cycle. At this stage, the Canton of Vaud system provides a skills analysis for the transition to upper secondary schools. Depending on the results, the student may access general education paths or vocational paths. This orientation moment is critical, as it determines the young person's future professional or academic career.
Another scenario concerns linguistic integration. If a child is not fluent in French, the cantonal school system must manage their integration through linguistic support, given that teaching takes place predominantly in this language. The system's ability to adapt to different linguistic levels is a determining factor for initial academic success.
Organization into cycles also allows for greater pedagogical flexibility, enabling teachers to adapt teaching methods to the needs of the class group, while maintaining the standards required by the cantonal curriculum. This balance between regulatory rigor and didactic adaptation is what characterizes the educational approach in Vaud.

Although specific details may vary depending on the municipality of residence, the general procedure follows these steps:
1. Age verification: Check the child's date of birth to determine the corresponding school cycle. 2. Contact with the municipal administration: Visit the competent office of the municipality of residence to report the presence of the minor. 3. Submission of documents: Provide the child's identity documents and, if available, the vaccination record or previous school certificates. 4. School assignment: Receive notification of the reference school based on the residential area. 5. Class placement: Participate in preliminary meetings with teachers to define the starting level, especially regarding languages.
### Tools and planning To correctly manage entry into the school system, it is advisable to regularly consult the official calendar of the Canton of Vaud. This tool allows you to anticipate registration deadlines and plan break periods. Attention to detail during the registration phase avoids delays in the child's placement and ensures that the educational path begins smoothly, respecting the timelines set by the cantonal cycles. Once registration is complete, constant monitoring of progress during each cycle will be the key to a fluid transition toward upper secondary education.

item.title: Vote 27 September: 63% no to neutrality
item.description: Gfs.bern survey: over 60% of voters intend to reject initiatives on neutrality and food security as of 27 September.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Over 60% of voters intend to reject both federal initiatives. - Sharp drop in support for neutrality and food security in early September. - Popular vote scheduled for September 27 in all Cantons.
## Key facts - Survey: according to the gfs.bern survey for SSR (SBC) - Referendum date: September 27 - Neutrality initiative: promoted by the Pro Suisse committee - Neutrality result: 63% opposed, 34% in favor - Food security result: 64% opposed, 33% in favor
A clear majority of the Swiss electorate is preparing to reject both texts submitted to the federal vote on September 27, according to the second survey conducted by the gfs.bern institute for the Swiss Broadcasting Corporation SBC. Indeed, over 60% of those interviewed declare their intention to vote no on both the neutrality proposal and the food security proposal. Support for both projects has visibly declined compared to the first survey conducted in early August. Had the consultation taken place in early September, 63% would have rejected the initiative titled 'Safeguarding Swiss neutrality', with a nine-point percentage jump in opposition. At the same time, the front of supporters has dropped by eight points, settling at 34%.
### The rejection of the Pro Suisse initiative The neutrality initiative, launched by the Pro Suisse committee, aims to directly enshrine the principle of a 'permanent and armed' Swiss neutrality in the Federal Constitution. However, the text faces strong cross-cutting opposition from almost all major Swiss political parties, from the Greens to the Liberals. Voters faithfully follow party lines: more than three-quarters of the supporters of these political forces declare a vote against. The rejection is particularly clear among Liberal Green voters, who reach 96% opposition. The Swiss People's Party (SVP) remains the only major party to formally support the proposal. Among its ranks, 77% of voters support the initiative, although the figure shows a nine-point percentage drop compared to the first survey. Independent voters have also changed their minds: 59% now reject the text, whereas a month earlier, more than half were in favor. Even among voters with a lower level of education, who were initially more inclined to vote yes, 54% now declare themselves opposed. The opposition to the initiative «For safe food» has developed with even greater rapidity on a federal scale. The text calls for incentives for plant-based food production to increase the country's food self-sufficiency rate, but it has been met with almost unanimous rejection. Currently, 64% of citizens oppose the measure, marking a 15-point increase in opponents, while support has dropped by 14 points to 33%. The Federal Parliament has rejected the proposal unanimously. Despite attempts by left-wing parties and the Liberal Greens to propose a counterproject, no alternative has found approval, leaving the text without institutional support.
On a geographical level, data collected by gfs.bern highlights a convergence between the different linguistic realities of the Confederation, an element closely monitored by federal offices such as UST/BFS and SECO in the analysis of civic sentiment. Regarding the neutrality initiative, in German-speaking Switzerland, 64% of respondents declare they want to vote no. In Romandy, opposition increases by 14 percentage points and reaches 63%. Italian-speaking Switzerland, on the other hand, shows a more balanced fracture: 48% supports the initiative promoted by Pro Suisse, compared to 47% opposed. For the food initiative, the no front dominates everywhere: opposition peaks at 66% in German-speaking Switzerland. Initially, Latin cantons had shown sympathy for the food text, but support has collapsed by 19 points in Romandy and by 16 points in Italian-speaking Switzerland. Rejection also crosses age groups: 58% of voters between 18 and 39 years old reject the food proposal, as do 59% of women. Among parties, while three-quarters of the Greens still vote in favor, support among socialists has slipped below 50%. Furthermore, the Liberal Greens have reversed their orientation: 52% now explicitly oppose the food measure.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). For residents called to the polls on September 27, the decisions on the two objects up for vote will have indirect repercussions on the overall framework of the Confederation, ranging from the debate on international relations led by the Federal Council to supply policies that may impact the [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living). According to analyses by the gfs.bern institute, a reversal of the trend on the Pro Suisse initiative would require a massive mobilization of the SVP (UDC) electorate combined with a radical shift in the rest of the population, a scenario for which the institute detects no signs. Even on the food front, urban and suburban areas have aligned with rural zones, which have historically been skeptical of production constraints aimed at the plant sector.
### Voting methods and civic tools Those entitled to vote in Switzerland receive the official postal voting material directly at their home in the various Cantons several weeks before the set date. The procedure for participating in the democratic consultation follows precise steps: - Receipt of the official envelope containing the Federal Chancellery’s information sheets, voting certificates, and ballot papers. - Manual completion of the ballot, expressing ‘Yes’ or ‘No’ for each of the two federal questions. - Signing the voting certificate in the designated space to validate the vote. - Sending the stamped envelope by post before the deadline indicated by your municipality, or direct delivery to the municipal chancery of residence by the closing time of the polling stations on September 27.

item.title: Permit L in Vaud: validity 1 year and renewal up to 24 months
item.description: The L permit lasts a maximum of 1 year, renewable for a second year. After 24 months it passes to permit B. Complete guide for the Canton of Vaud.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Permit L: maximum validity of 1 year - Renewable for a second year - Maximum total: 24 months - Switch to permit B after 2 years
## Key facts - Permit type: L (short duration) - Initial duration: up to 1 year - Renewal: possible for 1 year - Total duration max: 2 years - Next step: Permit B (residence) - Authority: SEM (Secretariat of State for Migration)
The short-term permit, known as the L permit, is the main instrument for third-country nationals who intend to work in Switzerland for a limited period. The State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) defines the federal guidelines, which are applied by the various Cantons, including the specific procedure in the Canton of Vaud. The distinctive feature of this permit is its temporary nature, designed for defined work projects or for probationary periods before a professional stabilization.
The standard validity of the L permit is set at one year. This term is not fixed but represents the maximum limit for the first issue. The employer must be the applicant for the procedure, ensuring that the workplace is real and compliant with labour market regulations. Once the first year has expired, the holder may request a renewal for a second year, provided that the employment relationship continues and that there are no substantial changes in the contractual conditions or in the personal situation of the worker.
### The structure The distinction between the L permit and the B permit is not merely formal but has direct practical implications for the daily life and financial planning of those living in Switzerland. While the L permit is strictly tied to a specific employment relationship, the B permit offers greater autonomy. However, the transition is not automatic: it requires a conversion procedure that must be initiated before the expiration of the second year of the L permit.
### Implications for social security and taxation
During the period of the L permit, the worker is subject to the same social security regulations as any other resident. AVS/AI/IPG contributions are mandatory, with a rate of 5.3% paid by the employee and the same amount paid by the employer, for a total of 10.6%. Unemployment insurance (AD/AC) and mandatory daily allowance insurance for sickness and maternity (LAINF/LAA) also apply, with rates varying between 0.7% and 1.5% depending on the sector.
Regarding professional pension schemes, the LPP/BVG comes into play for the portion of the salary that exceeds the coordination threshold. Contribution rates vary based on age: from 7% for those aged 25-34 up to 18% for those aged 55 and over. It is important to note that, despite being a short-term permit, work performed under an L permit generates social security contributions which, in the event of moving abroad, can be refunded or retained based on bilateral agreements.
On the fiscal level, a worker residing in Vaud is subject to the three-tier tax system: federal, cantonal, and communal. The Federal Tax Administration (AFC/ESTV) manages direct federal tax (IFD) and VAT, while cantonal and communal administrations apply their own multipliers. Residence in Switzerland, even temporary, triggers the obligation to file a tax return. The cost of living and budget management must take these withholdings into account, as they significantly impact the monthly net income.
### Transition scenarios
If the employer decides not to renew the contract at the end of the first year, the worker finds themselves in a delicate position. Without a new contract to justify the renewal of the L permit, residency is at risk. In such cases, the search for a new job must take place within the timeframes established by law to avoid losing the right of residence. The flexibility of the Swiss labor market, while high, does not automatically guarantee permit continuity if the employment link is broken. Advance planning, including verifying the requirements for a B permit, is recommended to avoid interruptions in social security and health coverage.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). To properly manage the transition from an L permit to a B permit, it is essential to adhere to precise timing. The conversion application must be submitted before the expiration of the second year of the L permit. Delaying this procedure may result in the loss of insurance coverage and the need to restart the process from the beginning.
### Step-by-step procedure
1. Document verification: ensure you have an updated employment contract, salary certificates, and proof of residence in Switzerland. 2. Application submission: contact the migration office of the Canton of Vaud with complete documentation. The employer must co-sign the request. 3. Health insurance: verify that your LAMal coverage is active and that the chosen deductible is adequate for your budget. Coverage is mandatory within 3 months of arrival and must remain valid throughout the entire period of residence. 4. Bank account: if you do not already have one, open an account in Switzerland to manage tax and social security withholdings. Current accounts are managed by national banks and must comply with anti-money laundering regulations.
### Useful tools for planning
To accurately calculate your net income and the taxes due in Vaud, it is useful to use tax simulation tools. These tools allow you to see how cantonal and municipal tax rates influence your payslip. Additionally, it is important to monitor the cost of living, which varies from one region to another, to adapt your standard of living to your net income.
Pension provision is another aspect to consider in the long term. Even if the L permit is short-term, contributions paid to LPP/BVG are accumulated and can be transferred or refunded according to federal laws. Always check the available options to avoid losing acquired rights.
For those in a transitional situation, the support of a tax consultant or a union can be valuable. However, the first line of defense remains understanding your legal and tax obligations. Switzerland offers a transparent system, but it requires that residents know the rules of the game.

The purchase of a home in the Canton of Zug has specific characteristics that affect naughty buyers and more. The real estate market in the canton of Ticino, already among the most expensive nationwide, requires a careful assessment of the resources needed to access a sustainable mortgage. The sustainability of the loan is assessed on the basis of the ratio between installments and disposable income, according to criteria established by the supervisory authorities and Swiss banking rules. ### Prices and Funds ## The Practical Impact of Tax and Banking Choices
Buying a home in the Canton of Zug requires planning that takes into account not only the property price but also all additional expenses. The property transfer tax, present in every Swiss canton, is regulated at the cantonal level with a multiplier that can vary between municipalities. This means the tax amount depends on the exact location of the property: two municipalities within the same canton may apply different rates. For the buyer, it is important to inquire at the relevant municipal administration before proceeding with the purchase.
Notary fees, on the other hand, are set at the federal level and do not vary between cantons. They include the cost of the notarial deed and related taxes, and are added to the purchase price of the home. This means that, in addition to the equity and mortgage, the buyer must consider an additional financial burden that is not always calculated upfront. The combination of property transfer tax and notary fees can represent a significant portion of the total cost, especially in a canton like Zug where real estate prices are already high.

The sustainability of the mortgage is a crucial aspect evaluated by Swiss banks when granting a loan. The required equity varies depending on the type of mortgage and the policy subscribed to, but generally, banks require a minimum that covers a significant portion of the property price.
This mechanism encourages the buyer to plan their resources in advance, evaluating the possibility of increasing available equity or reducing the mortgage request. Mortgage sustainability is not just a matter of amount: banks also assess income stability, the duration of the employment contract, and the ability to maintain installments even in the event of unforeseen circumstances. This prudent approach by the Swiss banking system aims to contain the risk of insolvency, protecting both the buyer and the bank itself.

item.title: Federal Council rejects the UDC initiative on borders
item.description: The Federal Council recommends rejecting the UDC initiative on borders. High costs, damage to the economy and risks for Schengen have been detected.
item.content:encoded:
## At a glance - The Federal Council rejects the SVP border initiative - High costs and damage to the Swiss economy identified - The executive warns of risks to Schengen and Dublin - Alternative measures on the way through the European Pact
## Key facts - Initiative: Stop abuses in asylum - Daily border crossings: 2.2 million - Cost of leaving Schengen: 5.8 to 16.1 billion - Maximum asylum limit: 5,000 people
The Federal Council has officially recommended that Parliament reject the popular initiative promoted by the SVP for border protection, formally named Stop abuses in asylum. The Swiss executive expressed a clear rejection of the proposal, highlighting a series of significant critical issues that could affect the entire national territory. According to the government's assessment, the implementation of the new measures would entail very high costs, a deterioration of the country's welfare, a weakening of internal security, and severe damage to Switzerland's traditional humanitarian policy. Furthermore, the executive reiterated that the text would not even be suitable for effectively curbing the phenomenon of irregular migration and cross-border crime. Specifically, the initiative requires systematically controlling all incoming people, fully manning border crossings, and turning back those who do not meet entry conditions, while introducing a maximum cap of 5,000 asylum grants per year. For those staying irregularly, the text requires a notification obligation, the nullity of employment contracts, exclusion from social and health insurance, and the obligation to leave the territory within 90 days.
### Impacts on daily mobility The repercussions of permanent and systematic controls would inevitably reflect on traffic and the management of Swiss customs checkpoints. The Confederation registers approximately 2.2 million border crossings daily and the presence of many hundreds of thousands of cross-border commuters. Consequently, the execution of fixed and systematic checks would heavily burden the national economy and traffic fluidity, generating billions of francs in congestion costs especially in border regions. The government emphasizes that it would be essential to significantly increase border protection personnel, generating a further increase in public spending. Current customs procedures, the executive recalls, are already based on checks tailored to the situation and risks, which can be intensified as needed without resorting to permanent blockades of internal borders. To delve deeper into the general economic impact and the management of daily expenses, you can consult the resources dedicated to the [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living) in Switzerland. ### Security and Schengen Consequences
A central aspect of the analysis conducted by the Federal Council concerns the strategic link between Switzerland and European cooperation agreements. Accepting the initiative would concretely jeopardize the Confederation's association with the Schengen and Dublin system. The potential abandonment of this regulatory and security framework would weaken the country's internal protection, as Switzerland would lose immediate access to shared European search databases. Furthermore, Swiss authorities would find themselves in a position of having to independently re-examine all applications rejected by other Dublin member states, without retaining the power to transfer applicants to the competent European countries. This situation would lead to a significant and predictable increase in the number of applications handled directly at the national level. To support this assessment, the government cites an official report commissioned by the National Council, according to which the annual costs resulting from the abandonment of Schengen and Dublin would range between a minimum of 5.8 billion and a maximum of 16.1 billion Swiss francs.
### Analysis of Quantitative and Humanitarian Limits
The proposal to set a maximum limit of 5,000 asylum grants per year conflicts with obligations arising from international law. To avoid violations of signed treaties, the Confederation would still be required to examine each individual asylum application separately, making it impossible to proceed with automatic rejection and repatriation of applicants. People fleeing armed conflict zones would no longer be able to obtain provisional admission, thus calling into question Switzerland's historic humanitarian tradition. On the integration front, the text under examination would make it almost impossible for individuals with prolonged stays to achieve financial independence, with the concrete risk of heavily overburdening cantonal structures dedicated to emergency relief. Nevertheless, the executive recognizes the need to intervene in the migration sector, aiming to curb secondary migration movements within the Schengen area through the coordinated application of measures provided for by the European Pact on Migration and Asylum, in which Switzerland actively participates.

In this scenario, the Federal Department of Justice and Police has initiated preparatory work to define, in close collaboration with the Cantons, new legislative amendments. The primary objective of these regulatory interventions is to tangibly relieve the national asylum system and overall raise security levels within the sector. The Cantons and federal authorities therefore continue to monitor the evolution of the regulatory framework, evaluating alternative administrative tools to address the challenges related to migration flows without compromising economic balances and the free movement of cross-border commuters. Final decisions will now be submitted to the Federal Parliament, which will have to discuss the rejection recommendation formulated by the executive and schedule the next institutional steps.
### Operational References for Citizens For those who live and work in Swiss territory, the evolution of the political and regulatory debate on security, cross-border commuting, and public finance requires constant monitoring of federal provisions. item.description: The Swiss National Bank is preparing for the economic exam with rates at 0.0% and inflation in Switzerland rising to 0.8% in August.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The SNB will hold its third annual review of the economic and monetary situation - Experts unanimous: policy rate will remain unchanged at 0.0% - Inflation in Switzerland rose to 0.8% in August - 2027 forecasts split between 0.0% and 0.75%
## Key facts - Institution: SNB - Review date: Thursday - Current policy rate: 0.0% - August inflation: 0.8% - July inflation: 0.4% - SNB target range: 0% and 2% - 2027 rate spread: 0.00 to 0.75% - Chairman of the institution: Martin Schlegel
The Swiss National Bank (SNB) is preparing for its third annual review of the economic and monetary situation, scheduled for Thursday in Bern. Economic experts are absolutely unanimous in believing that the policy rate will remain unchanged at 0.0% during this monetary policy appointment. Despite the recent increase recorded in Switzerland by inflation, which rose to 0.8% in August from 0.4% in July, analysts agree that there are currently no prerequisites for an immediate intervention on the cost of borrowing.
### The inflation and interest rate framework
The price increase recorded in recent months continues to remain stably within the target range defined by the SNB itself, specifically a band between 0% and 2%. Consequently, price dynamics show no alarm signals that would justify an immediate monetary tightening. The current situation sees the Swiss central bank moving in an international context characterized by different moves by other major global monetary authorities.
### Decisions of foreign central banks
Last week, the European Central Bank (ECB) proceeded with a rate hike, while this Wednesday the Federal Reserve implemented its first increase. Inevitably, faced with these international movements, the question that operators and analysts are asking concerns the future moves of the SNB in the coming months and quarters. Although Thursday's review holds no surprises regarding the current level of the policy rate, general attention inevitably shifts toward the coming quarters, where the real question for economists is no longer whether there will be interventions, but when they will be implemented. The estimates prepared by experts for the coming quarters and the end of 2027 diverge widely, drawing a range for the SNB's policy rate from 0.00% to 0.75%. This strong divergence of opinions among financial analysts highlights the uncertainty linked to the evolution of national and international macroeconomic factors in the coming years. The research institute BAK Economics hypothesizes a first increase in the cost of money as early as December, while other operators in the financial sector shift the forecast for the first increase starting from March 2027.
### Economic pressure factors
At the root of these upward forecasts are very precise elements: rising inflation, the trend towards a weaker franc, and the overall recovery of the economy. Under these operating conditions, the strongly expansionary stance of monetary policy adopted so far would no longer be considered necessary, making a gradual normalization of interest rates appropriate. In recent months, the Swiss currency has recorded a noticeable weakening that certainly offers a competitive advantage to the export economy, but at the same time makes imported goods decidedly more expensive, starting with energy.
### The impact of the franc and the SNB's reaction
A less strong franc generates inevitable additional inflationary pressure originating from abroad. As long as the Swiss currency maintains underlying robustness and domestic price increases remain low, the SNB can afford to keep the rate at 0.0%. However, the longer and more intensely the franc weakens, the greater the pressure on imported prices becomes. In this scenario, several specialists predict that the institution led by Martin Schlegel could primarily use foreign currency sales as a complementary intervention tool, favoring the appreciation of the franc and containing external inflationary pressure.
### The role of reserves and the rate differential
The management of the huge accumulated foreign exchange reserves offers the SNB considerable leeway to intervene in the currency markets. As Renato Flückiger of Valiant Bank points out, this aspect takes on particular significance in the event that the interest rate differential with cross-border countries should continue to widen further over the coming months.

item.title: Insurers: no recourse to the entire hospital list
item.description: The Federal Administrative Court dismissed the appeal of prio.swiss against the hospital list of the Canton of Switzerland. Only targeted appeals are possible.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Appeal dismissed by the Federal Administrative Court - Insurers cannot challenge the entire hospital list - It is only possible to appeal individual planning decisions - The court's decision is final and without appeal
## Key facts - Appellant body: Association of Swiss Health Insurers (prio.swiss) - Court: Federal Administrative Court (FAC) in St. Gallen - Canton concerned: Canton of Schwyz - Scope: List of hospitals for acute somatic care - Outcome: Appeal dismissed
Health insurers do not have the legal standing to file an appeal against a canton's hospital list in its entirety. In a published ruling, the Federal Administrative Court formally dismissed the application filed by the trade association. The legal dispute originated from the appeal submitted by the Association of Swiss Health Insurers (prio.swiss) to the Federal Administrative Court (FAC) in St. Gallen. The subject of the dispute concerned the list of hospitals for acute somatic care drawn up by the State Council of the Canton of Schwyz. Based on what emerged in the legal claims, the insurers sought the complete annulment of the hospital list. The claim put forward aimed to obtain the referral of the entire act to the Schwyz executive, so that the latter could proceed with the drafting of a new comprehensive hospital planning for the cantonal territory. However, the judges based in St. Gallen examined the issue and established an opposite principle, rejecting the request for total annulment.
### The assessment of the federal administrative judges
According to the orientation expressed by the Federal Administrative Court, a hospital list cannot in any way constitute the object of a global or collective challenge. In the grounds written in support of the judgment, the FAC clarified that a list of hospital facilities does not represent a single and indivisible administrative act. On the contrary, it constitutes a coordinated set of distinct service mandates entrusted to individual facilities operating within a canton, namely hospitals, maternity homes and nursing homes. For this reason, the judicial system excludes the possibility of contesting the entire planning framework with a single general appeal. Insurers nevertheless retain the prerogative to act in the appropriate venues, but through different methods compared to what was attempted against the Canton of Schwyz. The practical implications arising from the ruling of the Federal Administrative Tribunal outline a well-defined framework regarding the relations between trade associations in the insurance sector and cantonal governments on health matters. The decision establishes a clear line of demarcation on the methods for controlling regional hospital planning. Industry operators cannot undertake massive legal action to overturn the entire acute somatic care planning network decided by a cantonal executive. On the contrary, the protection of the economic and managerial interests of health insurers must necessarily take place through targeted and punctual challenges.
### Analysis of appeal procedures and operational alternatives
The procedural rules set by the judges in St. Gallen require insurers to change their strategy in examining the health planning measures issued by the Cantons. In detail, the possibility of using judicial instruments to contest cantonal administrative decisions must translate into the appeal of individual specific measures. When a trade association identifies critical issues in the distribution of service mandates, legal action cannot target the general act of the Council of State, but must focus on the individual mandates assigned to well-identified structures, such as specific hospitals, individual maternity homes, or individual nursing homes. This restrictive principle protects the stability of local public health planning, preventing entire lists of regional health structures from being blocked or called into question by a global appeal filed by insurance organizations. To verify how these dynamics reflect on the system and consult regulatory details or the overall impact on costs, it is useful to consult the overview on the cost of living in Switzerland (nav:cost-of-living) to have a clear picture of health and administrative expenses in the country.

The ruling issued by the Federal Administrative Court is final and binding on all the institutional actors involved. The judges of St. Gallen have expressly stressed that the decision is not susceptible to further encumbrance and cannot in any way be appealed before the Federal Court of Lausanne. This means that the judicial process for the global challenge of the cantonal hospital lists is definitively interrupted at the TAF level, confirming the restrictive orientation adopted regarding the right of appeal of trade associations.
### Procedure and limits for trade associations
For operators in the sector and trade associations that intend to monitor or challenge the health planning acts issued by the cantonal governments, the way forward requires a detailed and targeted analysis of the individual administrative measures. No collective action or general blocking of regional lists is allowed. The correct procedure requires isolating the individual decisions relating to the service mandates assigned to the individual health institutions in order to be able to initiate a specific judicial dispute. item.description: The association rejects any hypothesis of additional taxation on the profits of companies in the raw materials sector.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Suissenégoce rejects new profit taxes - Risk of oil shortage in Switzerland ruled out - 50% of the petrol price derives from taxes
## Key facts - Association: Suissenégoce - Sector: Commodity trading and shipping - Representative: Florence Schurch - Policy: Karin Keller-Sutter - Refinery: Cressier - Refinery coverage: 30%
Suissenégoce, the association of Swiss companies active in commodity trading and shipping, has expressed strong opposition against any hypothesis of additional taxation targeting the profits of companies in the sector. In an interview with the Awp agency, Secretary General Florence Schurch addressed recent political discussions and international economic tensions directly involving Switzerland.
Taxing the profits of companies active in the oil and commodity sector more heavily does not represent an effective solution, according to the association, since the companies involved already pay huge sums in taxes, quantifiable in hundreds of millions of francs. The head of the Federal Department of Finance, Karin Keller-Sutter, herself highlighted how the Confederation managed to close its budget thanks to the tax revenue generated in Geneva.
### The role of companies and pump prices
Companies in the sector operate on the global market and are remunerated for their brokerage and supply activities, but cannot be held responsible for world geopolitical events or fluctuations in fuel prices. The price applied at the petrol pump depends on multiple complex factors, including refining costs, transport expenses, the exchange rate and excise duties applied by government authorities. The tensions recorded in the Middle East have caused a drastic reduction in oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz and, more recently, through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, blocked by Houthi activities. Despite this complex scenario, there is no risk of energy shortages in Switzerland. This security is guaranteed on one hand by the country's accumulated strategic reserves and on the other by Switzerland's ability to absorb price increases with greater ease compared to other nations.
### Supply Strategies and Alternative Routes
When oil becomes less accessible in certain geographical areas, the task of traders consists in diversifying supply sources, turning to alternative producing countries such as Norway, Africa, or the United States. The real risk for the market is not the physical lack of the raw material, but rather the upward price dynamics due to lower global availability. Tariffs depend entirely on market trends and are subject to random factors that make it impossible to predict the maximum level prices could reach.
Regarding transport routes, logistical difficulties in the Persian Gulf force traders to transport oil by truck across the Arabian Peninsula to reach the Red Sea and load it onto ships, as the pipeline crossing Saudi Arabia has been hit by bombings. This extraordinary logistical chain and growing insurance costs inevitably contribute to pushing final energy prices upwards, while the duration of these price hikes represents the true critical issue for the economic system.

Swiss legislation provides specific tools to address emergency energy situations and market volatility. The country has strategic oil and gas reserves that can be activated in case of extraordinary need. A concrete example involves the Cressier refinery in the Canton of Neuchatel, which supplies about 30% of the national fuel demand and for which the Confederation recently authorized a withdrawal from strategic reserves to cope with transport difficulties.
### Mitigation measures and fuel taxation
The logistical situation is also aggravated by internal factors, such as water levels in the Rhine River that are too low to allow full loading of vessels used for the transport of fossil energy. In this context, if fuel prices were to rise excessively, the federal government has the power to intervene by reducing the tax burden on petroleum products. It is worth noting that about 50% of the total price of gasoline paid by consumers at the pump consists of state-determined taxes and excise duties.
Commodity trading companies continue to generate significant profits, but their logistical and commercial role ensures that the resident population can count on a constant energy supply, guaranteeing heating and mobility even during periods of international crisis. ## In a nutshell - Permit C: permanent residence for foreign residents in Switzerland - Requirements: 10 years of residence (5 for EU/EFTA citizens) - Key factors: integration, language and absence of social aid - Procedure: application submitted to the authorities of the Canton of Zug
## Key facts Permission: Address C Standard residence: 10 years EU/EFTA Residence: 5 years Canton of reference: Zug Requirements: Integration, language, financial stability
Residence permit C represents the highest degree of stability for a foreign citizen residing in the Canton of Zug and, more generally, in Swiss territory. This residence permit, managed according to the SEM directives, makes it possible to almost totally equate the rights of the resident with those of the Swiss citizen, eliminating the need for periodic renewals typical of the B permit. To obtain it, the applicant must meet strict criteria related to the length of stay and personal conduct.
### Time requirements and access The general rule is that a foreign national can apply for the C permit after 10 years of uninterrupted residence in Switzerland. However, for citizens belonging to the EU/EFTA States, this period is reduced to 5 years, facilitating access to permanent residence. In the Canton of Zug, as in the rest of the Confederation, obtaining this permit is not automatic, but depends on the verification of specific integration and stability criteria.
Integration Obtaining the C permit in the Canton of Zug brings significant changes to the resident's daily and legal life. One of the main advantages is independence from the employment contract: unlike the B permit, which is often linked to a specific employer or the availability of employment, the C permit does not expire and does not require the employment contract to be updated for its maintenance. This ensures greater professional flexibility and superior psychological security for those who decide to invest long-term in the canton's economic fabric.
### Tax and Social Security Implications From a tax perspective, a resident with a C permit is fully integrated into Switzerland's three-tier system: direct federal tax (managed by the AFC/ESTV), cantonal tax, and municipal tax. In the Canton of Zug, known for its competitive tax policy, the cantonal and municipal taxes are calculated by applying a specific multiplier, which varies depending on the municipality of residence. This system makes it essential to monitor one's tax residence to optimize the overall tax burden.
On the social security front, the holder of a C permit continues to pay mandatory AVS/AI/IPG contributions (5.3% borne by the employee) and unemployment insurance AD/AC. The stability of domicile also facilitates the planning of professional pension LPP/BVG, where contributions vary based on age (from 7% for 25-34 year olds up to 18% for those over 55). Those holding a C permit can also manage their third pillar 3a with greater peace of mind, an essential tool for reducing taxable income and supplementing future pensions. item.description: The Federal Council is asking for almost a billion extra francs for ground-to-air and radar systems to deal with threats in Europe.

## In brief - 970 million francs extra requested for the army - Funds for ground-to-air defense, radar, and anti-drone systems - Support for agriculture and security for international summits - Total projected expenditures of 1.068 billion francs
## Key Facts - Applicant: Federal Council - Army Amount: 970 million francs - Agriculture Amount: 54 million francs - Summit Security Amount: 20 million francs - Swiss Amount (overnight stays): 0.7 million francs - Total budget expenditures: 1.068 billion francs
The Federal Council has submitted a credit request to Parliament as part of the second supplementary budget, forecasting an increase of nearly one billion francs for the armed forces. This decision, already anticipated in August, responds to a worsening threat situation in Europe and strong tension affecting the armaments market. The executive's goal is to guarantee production capacities and ensure that delivery terms for systems deemed urgently necessary are respected, in line with the 2026 armament program.
### Detail of military investments
The breakdown of the 970 million francs allocated to the army is defined as follows: 650 million francs are planned for the purchase of medium-range ground-to-air defense systems, while 250 million are destined for short-range systems. A further 60 million francs will be used for the acquisition of a partially mobile medium-range radar, while 10 million francs are allocated for specific defense systems against mini-drones.
In addition to military spending, the government has requested further funds for various emergencies and commitments. 54 million francs have been allocated to support farms that suffered damage from drought during the summer. Regarding security linked to international events, 20 million francs are planned to cover 80% of the costs incurred by the Cantons of Geneva, Vaud, Valais, and Ticino for the G7 summit in Evian and the OSCE ministerial conference, which will be held in Lugano in December. Finally, 0.7 million francs are destined for Swiss company to reimburse the overnight stay expenses of air traffic security guards between 2016 and 2024. The impact of these decisions is directly reflected in the financial management of the Confederation and the organization of security in the involved Cantons. The Federal Council's request is not limited to immediate credits, but includes new commitment credits to allow the State to assume contractual obligations that extend beyond the current year. In particular, 100 million francs have been requested for urgent interventions in the real estate sector, aimed at improving the army's self-protection, 13.6 million for a portfolio management system for the Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (DDPS), and 15.8 million for the implementation of the cell broadcast alarm system.

For the residents and administrations of the Cantons of Ticino, Valais, Vaud, and Geneva, the federal intervention of 20 million francs represents a partial tax relief, covering 80% of the security costs for international summits. Without this contribution, the financial burden for organizing the OSCE conference in Lugano and the G7 in Evian would fall entirely on the cantonal budgets. This cost-sharing mechanism highlights how events of national or international importance require financial coordination between Bern and the Cantons.
On the infrastructural level, an additional credit of 5 million francs is planned for the Railway Infrastructure Fund (RIF), destined for the completion works of the New Railway Link through the Alps (NRLA). It is important to emphasize that this specific funding will not weigh on the Confederation's budget, as it is guaranteed directly by the RIF. This scenario differs from the credits for the army or agriculture, which instead impact State expenditures. From an accounting point of view, considering a credit carry-over of 23.6 million francs from 2025, the overall operation of the second supplement will lead to increased expenditures of 1.068 billion francs. item.title: Permit L in Vaud: validity max 1 year and extension
item.description: Validity up to 1 year, employer constraint and SEM management. The rules for the extension or transition to permit B.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Short-term L permit: maximum validity of up to 1 year - Restriction: tied to a specific employer - Possibility of extension or transition to a B residence permit - Managed by the SEM at the federal level and applied in the Canton of Vaud
## Key facts Permit: Short-term L permit Maximum validity: 1 year Federal authority: SEM Territorial scope: Canton of Vaud Type: Tied to employer Possible evolution: B permit
The short-term L permit in the Canton of Vaud represents an administrative solution for temporary stays, with a validity that can last up to a maximum of one year. This residence title is strictly linked to the employment relationship that enabled its issuance, creating a direct bond between the foreign worker and the specific employer. The management of such permits falls under the jurisdiction of the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) at the federal level, although practical application and issuance are carried out through the cantonal authorities of Vaud.
### Characteristics and limits of the L permit The temporary nature of this permit implies that it is not intended for those seeking immediate stable residence, but for those undertaking fixed-term assignments. The one-year time limit is mandatory for the initial validity. Since the permit is tied to the employer, the potential termination of the contractual relationship before the expiration of the title may affect the validity of the stay itself. Holders of an L permit must also comply with legal obligations for residents, including the obligation to take out LAMal health insurance within three months of arriving in Switzerland. This insurance is private, with per capita premiums that vary depending on the canton and region, and offers several deductible options for adults (300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, or 2500 CHF). Regarding social security, the worker is subject to AVS/AI/IPG contributions, with a rate of 5.3% borne by the employee and a total of 10.6% including the employer's share. [Living in Switzerland](nav:living-ch) also involves adherence to LPP for coordinated salary, with rates that vary based on the worker's age: from 7% for the 25-34 age bracket up to 18% for those over 55 years old up to the reference age. The analysis of the transition from the short-term L permit to more stable residence permits reveals precise dynamics in the Canton of Vaud. The extension of the L permit is possible, but remains subject to the conditions of the employment contract and the evaluations of the migration authorities. The transition to the B residence permit, which is renewable and offers greater flexibility, represents the goal for many workers wishing to stabilize their professional and personal position in Swiss territory.
### Transition scenarios and employment constraints In a hypothetical scenario, a worker with an L permit who receives a proposal for a contract renewal on an indefinite basis or for a significantly longer period could request the conversion of their permit into a B permit. Conversely, if the employment contract expires and is not renewed, the L permit cannot be automatically extended, as the link with the employer is the cornerstone of its validity.
The comparison between the different permits highlights how the L permit is the first step of a ladder leading to the B permit and, subsequently, to the C settlement permit. The latter is generally accessible after 10 years of residence, a term that is reduced to 5 years for EU/EFTA citizens. It is important to consider that the entire Swiss tax structure applies to those residing with an L permit: taxation occurs on three levels, namely the direct federal tax (DFT), the cantonal tax, and the municipal tax. While the AFC/ESTV manages the DFT and VAT, the cantonal administrations handle the collection of cantonal and municipal taxes, where the latter apply a multiplier to the cantonal value. Those holding an L permit and receiving a salary must also pay unemployment insurance AD/AC at 1.1% up to the annual maximum and accident insurance LAINF/LAA with rates between 0.7% and 1.5% depending on the sector of activity. This system of contributions ensures basic social coverage, coordinated at the federal level by the UFAS/BSV, which however has no competence in setting taxes. [health insurance](nav:health) and social security are therefore mandatory pillars that accompany every phase of the stay, regardless of the duration of the permit.

To correctly manage the validity and any potential extension of the L permit in the Canton of Vaud, it is necessary to follow a rigorous administrative procedure. The first step consists of monitoring the expiration date of the residence permit, as the request for extension or change of permit must be submitted well in advance to the competent cantonal authorities.
### Operational procedure for renewal 1. Verification of remaining duration: check the expiration date on the L permit (maximum 1 year). 2. Alignment with the employer: obtain an extension of the employment contract or a confirmation of permanent employment to support the request for a B permit. 3. Document collection: prepare the documents required by the canton, including updated contracts and proof of accommodation. 4. Submission of the application: send the request for extension or conversion to the migration offices of the Canton of Vaud. 5. Waiting for the notice: await the decision of the SEM and the cantonal authorities regarding the validity of the new permit.
During this process, it is useful to plan the financial impact related to the cost of living and taxes. ## In brief - Severe increase in housing shortage - Lowest point overcome - 45,000 units in 2026 - 50,000 units in 2027
## Key facts - Study published by: Wüest Partner - Net increase in 2024: 40,000 homes according to FSO - Estimated increase for 2025: 39,000 homes - Forecast for 2026: around 45,000 housing units - Forecast for 2027: around 50,000 housing units
In a context characterised by strong population growth in Switzerland, a significant housing shortage is currently being recorded, but the situation may improve soon, at least in some regions of the country. This is the main conclusion of a study published by the Wüest Partner real estate consultancy firm. According to the research, the lowest point in housing construction in Switzerland should now have been overcome. The company is forecasting around 45,000 housing units in 2026 and around 50,000 housing units in 2027.
To provide a direct comparison, it is worth looking at the data provided by the Federal Statistical Office (FSO), according to which the net increase in 2024 was only 40,000 homes. As for the current year, 2025, the estimates produced by Wüest Partner indicate a further decline to just 39,000 homes, effectively representing the lowest level recorded since 2009. This prolonged slowdown has exacerbated tensions in the Swiss real estate market, pushing up demand and drastically reducing the options available to those looking for a home.
### The causes of the construction slowdown
The sharp increase in housing production expected in the coming years should at least slightly alleviate the housing shortage throughout Switzerland by the end of 2027. According to Wüest Partner's analysis, the concrete foundations for this future recovery were laid several years ago. In 2020, vacant apartments, which had increased for consecutive years, began to decline rapidly. At the same time, the market value of residential properties rose sharply.
These favourable market conditions created strong incentives for new housing projects, stimulating further real estate development initiatives. However, from the initial project to the delivery of the finished house, several years regularly pass. Among the main reasons for this wait are the increased complexity in planning and building new homes caused by additional building regulations, rising construction costs and interest rate trends. These factors have temporarily acted as a brake on the sector, but in the meantime many projects developed since 2020 have passed the preliminary stages and are now in an advanced phase, close to completion. The recovery of the real estate and construction market will not be distributed uniformly across the entire national territory, but will follow a gradual and differentiated progression depending on the region. In fact, during 2026, the recovery will remain predominantly localized at the regional level. Housing production is expected to exceed the long-term average, particularly in individual cantons of French-speaking Switzerland and Alpine regions, offering a first glimmer of relief in well-defined geographical areas.
The situation is destined to evolve further in the following year. In 2027, the recovery will clearly gain greater geographical breadth, involving a larger number of territories. In particular, a strong increase in the number of available housing units is expected in Thurgau, Geneva, Valais, and Neuchâtel. Large parts of the Swiss Plateau should also significantly benefit from this positive development, offering new opportunities for those seeking stable housing solutions.
### Regional differences and prospects in major centers
Despite growth forecasts for 2026 and 2027, significant territorial disparities persist that require attention. In approximately half of Swiss cantons, housing production will continue to remain below the long-term average. Real estate experts strongly emphasize that a generalized easing of housing tensions is not yet on the horizon for the entire country.
The situation is expected to remain particularly difficult and complex, especially in major urban centers, where demographic pressure and housing demand remain high. Furthermore, a key point highlighted by analysts concerns current construction applications: these do not currently forecast further acceleration in housing production for 2028, confirming that the market must proceed with caution and that normalization will take time.
